# Reading: question-specific routines from the 2026 strategy guide

**Source:** [The Only IELTS Reading Strategy You Need in 2026](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Kch2Tb_T2Pg), video ID `Kch2Tb_T2Pg`. Full auto-generated English captions were exported and reviewed through 30:19. This guide overlaps the playlist Reading course and the channel’s twelve-question-types lesson; it adds a sharper “locate first, decide second” routine and a few question-order suggestions.

## Common decision routine

For tasks that require a specific detail, read the prompt and instructions first, predict the information or word form that would fit, and think of likely paraphrases. Scan to locate a likely passage; only then close-read that part and decide. The instructor calls this “where before what.” It reduces aimless full-text rereading, but is a classroom routine rather than a rule for every question. Always follow the task’s actual instructions and word limit. ([0:24–5:11](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Kch2Tb_T2Pg&t=24s))

- **Sentence completion:** read the incomplete sentences, predict the content and grammatical form, scan for a likely location, then check the source wording and spelling. ([0:29–3:12](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Kch2Tb_T2Pg&t=29s))
- **Summary, table, and flow-chart completion:** inspect the summary or diagram for context and grammar clues; use those to locate the relevant section; copy the source words accurately and check the stated limit. Questions may be answered with words from the passage or from a supplied list, so read the actual instructions. ([3:12–5:11](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Kch2Tb_T2Pg&t=192s); [25:48–26:56](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Kch2Tb_T2Pg&t=1548s))
- **Multiple choice:** read the stem and options closely enough to know how they differ; skim for the text’s broad meaning, locate the relevant evidence for each item, and close-read before choosing. Eliminate options the text rules out; if two remain, compare their exact difference against the evidence. ([5:11–8:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Kch2Tb_T2Pg&t=311s))
- **Short answer:** understand the question before scanning; underline useful anchors such as names, places, or objects, consider paraphrases, then read the located passage carefully and write only what answers the question. ([8:37–10:37](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Kch2Tb_T2Pg&t=517s))
- **Diagram labels:** use the title, labels, arrows, and word limit to understand the visual; do not assume specialist knowledge is being tested. Connect the diagram to the passage, locate the description, and check the copied answer. ([10:37–12:13](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Kch2Tb_T2Pg&t=637s))

## Questions that require a meaning judgment

- **True / False / Not Given:** read the whole statement, identify its meaning, anticipate paraphrases, and compare it with the relevant evidence. “False” requires contradiction; “Not Given” means the passage neither confirms nor contradicts the statement. Do not make a decision from one matching keyword, outside knowledge, or the assumption that each label must appear a set number of times. ([12:13–17:36](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Kch2Tb_T2Pg&t=733s); [official Academic Reading format](https://ielts.org/take-a-test/test-types/ielts-academic-test/ielts-academic-format-reading))
- **Yes / No / Not Given:** use the same evidence discipline, but judge the writer’s stated view or claim, not merely a factual event or another person’s opinion. ([17:36–19:41](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Kch2Tb_T2Pg&t=1056s); [official Academic Reading format](https://ielts.org/take-a-test/test-types/ielts-academic-test/ielts-academic-format-reading))
- **Matching sentence endings:** read the beginnings and predict a possible completion, then check the text. Grammar or personal logic alone cannot establish the answer. Cross out endings contradicted by the passage and compare the remaining meaning against evidence. ([19:41–21:12](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Kch2Tb_T2Pg&t=1181s))

## Matching tasks and order suggestions

- **Names/features:** scan for each name and mark every occurrence before matching it to a claim. The instructor suggests starting with names mentioned only once, then removing completed options to reduce clutter. This can help on some texts; it is not a universal priority rule, and one name may appear in more than one relevant place. ([21:12–23:22](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Kch2Tb_T2Pg&t=1272s))
- **Matching information:** read the statements, note possible paraphrases, skim the whole text for structure, then locate each statement and verify it against the paragraph. The instructor recommends doing it after other questions on that passage because those questions may build familiarity with the text. Use that order only if it saves time for the learner. ([23:22–25:48](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Kch2Tb_T2Pg&t=1402s))
- **Matching headings:** focus on each paragraph’s main idea rather than its first/last sentence or isolated keywords. The instructor’s method is to read each paragraph and write a plain-language heading before looking at the options; then compare the meanings and read more closely when several options remain. He recommends doing headings first because the task requires reading the whole passage. Treat both the order and the learner-generated heading as optional scaffolds. ([26:56–30:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Kch2Tb_T2Pg&t=1616s))

## Official check and limits

IELTS’s current Academic Reading guide separately labels matching information, matching headings, matching features, matching sentence endings, sentence completion, summary/note/table/flow-chart completion, diagram label completion, and short answers, alongside multiple choice and the two Not Given formats. The video’s “12 types” grouping splits or names some families differently; use its methods by task demand and teach the current official labels from the test format guide. The page confirms the False/Not Given and Yes/No/Not Given distinction and that instructions and word limits matter. ([IELTS Academic Reading format](https://ielts.org/take-a-test/test-types/ielts-academic-test/ielts-academic-format-reading))

Its promised Band 9 outcomes, “exact” methods, claims about which question is hardest or most common, and promotion of a free challenge/VIP course are not independently verified. Use the examples to teach reading decisions, not as a score guarantee. After a timed set, review each answer against the passage and classify the cause—task method, question interpretation, paraphrase, evidence location, word limit, spelling, or time—before choosing the next practice task. ([0:00–0:24](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Kch2Tb_T2Pg&t=0s); [30:00–30:19](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Kch2Tb_T2Pg&t=1800s))
